raised_and_not_decided_here.question: E01 counts every 1.01 without confirmation, as the approved definition specifies. In these seven windows eleven of the thirteen 1.01 items are debt agreements, one is Southwest's cooperation agreement with Elliott and one is Lumen's sale of its fiber business to AT&T.
raised_and_not_decided_here.why_it_is_separate: it is a question about the definition, not about the 8.01 branch: the route does exactly what the definition says for 1.01. E05 is the 1.01 count. If the owner wanted E01 restricted to M&A for 1.01 too, Ford would read 0, Lumen 1, Macy's 0 and Southwest 0.

recommendation.what_it_would_not_change: the frozen router and the ordinary route: #47 would carry the rule in its own generation, as it did for the D01 underline repair, and the two routes would differ on E01 until an issue_28-compatible generation carries the same rule.
recommendation.why: it is the only reading under which every count here is what the filings report: the one acquisition counts and the financing does not. B keeps the approved mechanism and applies it where the definition says, but the definition's own mechanism is what produces three false announcements out of four; A is honest about the route but deletes a clause the owner approved. C's weakness is its evidence base - one positive - and the plan answers it by recording every declined alias hit.

the_missing_meaning_judgement: Does an item 8.01 whose text uses one of the aliases only in a financing context - a use-of-proceeds list ('may include ... acquisitions'), a tender offer's 'combined aggregate purchase price' - confirm an M&A announcement? The approved match mode, a substring anywhere in the text, says yes; the metric's name says no. In this corpus the two disagree on three of the four 8.01 items that carry an alias. A second, smaller question rides with it: whether another item's text in the same filing (Item 1.01 covenants, Item 7.01) can confirm the 8.01.

what_the_route_does: deterministic_router.adapt_8k_item_index sets each claim's brief to '8-K item <code> parsed from hdr.sgml' whenever hdr.sgml carries item codes, and match_event_claims tests the aliases against that brief. Every filing in the seven windows has hdr item codes, so no 8.01 is ever admitted and the published E01 is the count of 1.01 and 2.01 items. The router is frozen by the issue_28 generations and shared with the ordinary route, which behaves the same way.
